engine_name: What a settled distinction changes elsewhere in the argument
problematique: A distinction or an encounter has settled (the owner's answer, the S1 rows): re-read the whole argument — every part, his and the desk's drafts, and his hunches — for what it changes: the parts it moves, supports, complicates or contradicts, the parts that rest on those and so change at one remove, and the tests that must run again (a hunch, a reference re-read, a frame). Structure alone cannot see this reach; the reading must (the owner, 2026-09-07 15:55: a change to the higher or lower parts of the stack has repercussions that must be ironed out sooner).
researcher_question: Given what the owner has just settled, which parts of his argument change, which change at one remove, and what must be re-tested?
